newsitem.title: USA: Inventor sues United Technologies automotive unit.
newsitem.headline: Inventor sues United Technologies automotive unit.

text.p: The inventor of a vehicle alarm system has sued the United Technologies Automotive Inc (UTA) unit of United Technologies Corp for allegedly infringing his patent for "Wireless Alarm System in Conjunction with at least One Vehicle."

In papers filed last week in the U.S. District Court in Delaware, George Fulhorst, who does business as Saf-T-Net USA, said that when he offered to license his patent to United Technologies Automotive in Dec 1995, the company turned him down.
The lawsuit claims "it was evident (in Dec 1995) that UTA was using the patented technology in connection with parts it was supplying to one or more major automakers."

But according to Fulhorst's lawsuit, UTA said there was no infringement "since UTA did not manufacture the vehicle horn or ignition circuit with which its alarm component was especially adapted to operate."
The vehicle alarm system works by activating horns and other alarm devices when someone presses a button on a portable transmitter or remote control.

Fulhorst, of Santa Clara, Calif., received his '178 patent in 1985. He told Reuters that the patent currently has no licensees and that similar lawsuits are being filed against four other manufacturers in other jurisdictions. Fulhorst has asked for a court order prohibiting further alleged infringement and for an award of triple damages for "willful and wanton" conduct.
Fulhorst's attorney in Houston was not available for comment. A spokesman for United Technologies Automotive in Dearborn said the company had not seen the lawsuit.
